episodes.165851: As a strong thunderstorm pushed offshore of the coast at the Cape in Brevard County, it produced a strong wind gust.
episodes.165962: A closed upper level low, and an accompanying surface low, approached the region from the west during the afternoon and evening.  Moderate instability associated with the combination of warm surface temps and cold temps aloft, in addition to moderate deep layer atmospheric shear and low freezing levels, led to an isolated severe thunderstorm that produced large hail in the CSRA.
episodes.165963: A closed upper level low, and an accompanying surface low, approached the region from the west during the afternoon and evening.  Moderate instability associated with the combination of warm surface temps and cold temps aloft, in addition to moderate deep layer atmospheric shear and low freezing levels, led to a few severe thunderstorms that produced large hail.
episodes.166432: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms developed across east-central Florida, with several becoming severe. These severe storms produced large hail in Brevard, Seminole, and Volusia County, with wind damage to trees also occurring in Volusia County.
episodes.166433: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms developed across east-central Florida, with storms moving offshore over the coast in Brevard and Volusia Counties. These storms produced numerous strong wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.166513: Showers and a few thunderstorms developed across north Alabama.  One of the showers produced a funnel cloud near Hartselle in Morgan County.
episodes.166561: A strong slow moving cold front pushed through Florida starting on the late evening of the 15th and going through the 16th. The front produced strong marine wind gust and a waterspout.
episodes.166562: A strong cold front continued to slowly push through Florida during tthe day causing a tornado in Sarasota County.
episodes.166913: A warm front lifted northward across southeast South Carolina in the morning ahead of an approaching low pressure system. The low, and associated cold front, gradually moved toward the area through the afternoon and eventually passed through and off the coast by the late evening hours. Thunderstorms impacted southeast South Carolina through much of the day, with a few of the thunderstorms becoming strong enough to produce penny to quarter sized hail.
episodes.166914: A warm front lifted northward across southeast Georgia in the morning ahead of an approaching low pressure system. The low, and associated cold front, gradually moved toward the area through the afternoon and eventually passed through and off the coast by the late evening hours. Thunderstorms impacted southeast Georgia through much of the day, with a few of the thunderstorms becoming strong enough to produce large hail.
episodes.167217: Strong thunderstorms developed over the area and produced large hail in southwest Alabama.
episodes.167654: Warm, moist, and unstable air ahead of a low pressure system and associated cold front across the SE U.S. and Gulf of Mexico promoted the development of strong thunderstorms across parts of SE Florida during the afternoon hours of March 16th.
episodes.168017: A low pressure system moved across north central AL with a warm front situated across central Georgia, supporting development of diurnally driven thunderstorms during the afternoon of March 16th. With modest CAPE values in combination with steep low and mid level lapse rates, there were multiple reports of hail ranging from quarter to golf ball size across portions of central Georgia.
episodes.168227: An upper-level low pressure center moved eastward across Central Alabama on Wednesday, March 16th, bringing showers and thunderstorms to portions of the area. Early in the afternoon, slow-moving thunderstorms developed over the Birmingham metro area and produced very heavy rainfall. Water quickly covered several roads, making them impassable. Multiple water rescues were conducted, and there was one fatality. Radar estimated that 2 to 4 inches of rain fell over the Birmingham metro area. A severe storm also developed over Lee County in the early afternoon that produced large hail.

Numerous roads were impassible and vehicles were flooded in the downtown area and near the University of Alabama-Birmingham campus.
